input.command:
cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --milestone "v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down" --label "bug,documentation,priority/P2" --title "docs: Ask AI → ChatGPT still fails — the prompt names the Markdown copy, which ChatGPT's reader rejects" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What
Ask AI → ChatGPT on the published docs still fails after #2245. ChatGPT replies (user report, 2026-09-30):

> The documentation page itself wasn't retrievable as Markdown by my web reader (the server returns an unsupported text/markdown content type), so I wouldn't attribute a specific reverse-proxy configuration to the DataQ docs without seeing that section.

## Why
#2245 made the prompt lead with the page's HTML URL but kept "(a plain Markdown copy is at …/index.md)". ChatGPT goes for the Markdown URL anyway, and GitHub Pages serves it as `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, a content type its reader rejects. It then reports the failure instead of answering from the HTML page. Verified live: the deployed ChatGPT link carries both URLs, the `.md` returns `text/markdown`, and the HTML page returns `text/html`. We can't set response headers on GitHub Pages.

## Fix
Give each assistant its own prompt. ChatGPT gets only the HTML page URL; Claude and GitHub Copilot keep the Markdown copy, which they read.

## Acceptance
- The generated ChatGPT link contains no `.md` URL; the Claude and Copilot links are unchanged.
- After the docs deploy, Ask AI → ChatGPT on a page answers from the page (a manual check; it can't be automated from here).
EOF

"""Unit tests for the curated docs catalog (no DB, no network) — #1626."""

from backend.app.mcp import docs_catalog


def test_list_pages_finds_the_top_level_pages() -> None:
    pages = docs_catalog.list_pages()
    for slug in (
        "best-practices",
        "feature-matrix",
        "security",
        "getting-started",
        "mcp-setup",
        "mcp-honesty",
        "evidence-card",
    ):
        assert slug in pages


def test_list_pages_finds_all_five_compliance_pages() -> None:
    """A glob/path bug here would silently drop pages rather than error — this
    is what catches that, not a hand-maintained slug list drifting (#1626).
    """
    pages = set(docs_catalog.list_pages())
    for slug in (
        "compliance/breach-notification-runbook",
        "compliance/data-subject-rights-runbook",
        "compliance/dpa-baa-templates",
        "compliance/dpia-input-sheet",
        "compliance/sub-processors",
    ):
        assert slug in pages


def test_list_pages_excludes_adrs_and_architecture() -> None:
    """The curated allowlist deliberately excludes contributor-facing docs —
    scanning a specific set of files/dirs, not a blanket docs/site walk.
    """
    pages = set(docs_catalog.list_pages())
    assert not any(p.startswith("adr/") for p in pages)

"""Published pages that state the MCP tool count must match the server (#2289)."""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from backend.tests.support.mcp_gates import GATES

_SITE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "docs" / "site"

# Pages that state the CURRENT count. ADRs and the changelog record historical counts on purpose.
_PAGES = (
    "guides/mcp-setup.md",
    "reference/glossary.md",
    "reference/feature-matrix.md",
    "get-started/ask-assistant.md",
)

_COUNT = re.compile(r"\b(\d+) (?:curated )?tools\b")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", _PAGES)
def test_a_published_tool_count_matches_the_server(page: str) -> None:
    counts = [int(n) for n in _COUNT.findall((_SITE / page).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]

    assert counts, f"{page} no longer states a tool count; drop it from _PAGES"
    assert set(counts) == {len(GATES)}
EOF

I found four problems in PR #2290: three published pages still state an old MCP tool count, and the new test cannot catch them. The server has 52 tools (checked against the tool registry, 28 read-only, 18 that change state, 6 live-probe).

1. `docs/site/guides/features.md:237` still says "The 48 split three ways: 25 read-only, 18 that change state, and 5 …". It should say 52, split 28/18/6.
2. `docs/site/operate/runbook-faq.md:81` still says "47 MCP tools at `/mcp`".
3. `docs/site/security/compliance/sub-processors.md:37` still says "via the 48 `/mcp` tools". This page is a compliance disclosure, so the size of the tool surface matters there.
4. `backend/tests/mcp/test_published_tool_count.py:20`: the test only checks four pages, and its pattern only matches "N tools" or "N curated tools".
   - It misses wordings like "N MCP tools" and "N `/mcp` tools".
   - It never checks the three-way split, so a stale glossary split (28/18/6) would still pass after a tool is added.
   - All three stale pages above exist at this commit and the test passes.

The other changes are fine. The deployment-parity page now says the two clouds were verified on the 48-tool surface, which is a correct historical statement rather than a stale count.

I posted finding 4 as an inline comment (https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2290#discussion_r4141971768). The other three are on files the PR doesn't change, so they went into one general PR comment instead (https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2290#issuecomment-5906385561).

content.content:
### Workspace membership: the next deploy must go through the workflow

The `workspace_members` migration and the code that reads it are on `main` in
separate steps and neither has rolled yet. The Deploy workflow runs
`alembic upgrade head` **before** it rolls images, so a normal deploy is safe in
either order. A hand-rolled image roll — `az containerapp update`, or a revision
rollback — ahead of the migration is not: the app would find no table.

CREATE ROLE dataq_app LOGIN PASSWORD '<generated>';
CREATE DATABASE dataq OWNER dataq_app;
-- then, connected to the `dataq` database (PG15+ doesn't grant the db owner
-- CREATE on public by default):
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO dataq_app;
ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO dataq_app;
```

Pass that password at apply time as `TF_VAR_app_db_password` (it becomes the
`DATABASE_URL` Container App secret; never committed). The app reaches the server
at runtime over the server's allow-Azure-services firewall rule.

## Apply

```bash
cd deploy/terraform/azure
tofu init
# image_tag / frontend_image_tag have no default: pass what prod runs NOW, so any
# app the apply creates (e.g. dataq-app-beat, #1811) starts on the live image.
IMG=$(az containerapp show -n dataq-app-worker -g dataq-rg --query 'properties.template.containers[0].image' -o tsv)
FE=$(az containerapp show -n dataq-app-frontend -g dataq-rg --query 'properties.template.containers[0].image' -o tsv)
TF_VAR_app_db_password='REDACTED' tofu plan -out=azure.plan \
  -var="image_tag=${IMG##*:}" -var="frontend_image_tag=${FE##*:}"   # review
tofu apply azure.plan
```

## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` reads these. Push them with `gh` from the outputs:

```bash

## Apply

```bash
cd deploy/terraform/aws
tofu init
# state_encryption_passphrase comes from your terraform.tfvars — see
# terraform.tfvars.example.
#
# Image tags (#1349): the services RUN these images from the first apply.
# publish-images.yml tags main merges as `main-<full sha>` (the bare `<sha>`
# tag is owned by the manual Azure deploy.yml and usually does NOT exist), and
# its `paths` filter skips merges that don't change image content — so use the
# last IMAGE-BEARING main commit, not the branch tip, and verify the tag
# exists before applying:
IMG_SHA=$(git log origin/main -1 --format=%H -- backend frontend pyproject.toml)
docker manifest inspect "ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:main-${IMG_SHA}" > /dev/null  # must succeed
TF_VAR_app_db_password="REDACTED" \
tofu plan -input=false -out=tfplan \
  -var="image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}" \
  -var="frontend_image_tag=main-${IMG_SHA}"
tofu apply -input=false tfplan
```

**Cost starts here.** `tofu apply` creates real, billable AWS resources (Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB). Review the plan before applying. See the root-level deployment plan (in the session that built this stack) for the cost breakdown against the AWS free-tier credit.

> **Existing stack picking up a new service (e.g. `beat`, #1811)?** `tofu apply` first — the
> Deploy workflow only rolls images onto services that already exist, it never creates them.
> Applying registers `aws_ecs_service.beat` (family `dataq-app-beat`, fixed name, no new repo
> variable needed — `deploy-aws.yml` references it the same way it references the other three)
> **before** the next `deploy-aws.yml` dispatch tries to `update-service` it.

content.text:
Both plans are ready. Nothing has been applied or deployed yet.

**Azure:** no infrastructure drift; the only change is one output value. No `tofu apply` is needed, only the Deploy workflow.

**AWS:** the plan is 4 to add, 1 to change, 1 to destroy.
- It creates the separate Celery `beat` service (task definition, log group and service). AWS has never had it; Azure got it on 09-27.
- It replaces the worker's task definition to drop `-B`, the embedded beat. The live AWS worker still runs `-B`. A plain apply would leave it there and start a second scheduler. Worse, `ecs_roll.sh` copies the latest worker revision into every future deploy, so the `-B` would never go away. The "destroy" is the old worker revision being deregistered; its running tasks keep running until the worker is updated.
- It updates the GitHub deploy role's policy to cover the new `beat` service.
- The DB password is carried over from the existing secret, so the database itself isn't touched.

**Proposed sequence:**

| Step | Cloud | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | AWS | `tofu apply tfplan` (images stay on the current `aws-7a3244a4`) |
| 2 | AWS | Immediately point the worker service at its new revision without `-B`, so two schedulers overlap for only a minute or two. The job that dispatches scheduled runs locks each schedule row, so a duplicate tick can't dispatch a run twice. |
| 3 | AWS | Dispatch `deploy-aws.yml` on `9f5475b7`: 16 migrations, then roll api, worker, beat and frontend |
| 4 | Azure | Dispatch `deploy.yml` on `9f5475b7`: 6 migrations, then roll all four apps |
| 5 | Both | Read `alembic_version` back on each database, check the image SHA on all four services per cloud, run the public smoke checks and an authenticated write probe |
| 6 | AWS | Run the DMF backfill (#2112): a dry run, then `--apply`. It already ran on Azure. |
| 7 | Both | Walk every feature on the #2224 checklist, log each step in `docs/ops-log.md`, and file anything found |

**Things to know before you approve:**
- **Databricks:** the ops log says the QA token must be rotated before today (09-30). The Unity Catalog checks may need a new token from you.
- **Snowflake:** its PATs expire on 10-11, so they're fine for this.
- **Write probes:** AWS has PATs stored in SSM. For Azure I'll need an admin PAT; I can mint one through the migrate-job override, which is a prod write, so I'll ask you at that point.

Approve steps 1–4, i.e. the AWS apply and both deploys?

"""Post-deploy smoke + authenticated probes. FE and PAT come from the environment."""

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

FE = os.environ["FE"].rstrip("/")
PAT = os.environ.get("PAT", "")
EXPECT_TOOLS = int(os.environ.get("EXPECT_TOOLS", "52"))
fails: list[str] = []


def req(method, path, *, auth=False, body=None, headers=None, raw_url=None):
    h = dict(headers or {})
    if auth:
        h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {PAT}"
    data = None
    if body is not None:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        h.setdefault("Content-Type", "application/json")
    r = urllib.request.Request(raw_url or FE + path, data=data, method=method, headers=h)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=60) as resp:
            return resp.status, dict(resp.headers), resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, dict(e.headers), e.read()


def check(label, cond, detail=""):
    print(f"{'PASS' if cond else 'FAIL'}  {label}  {detail}")
    if not cond:
        fails.append(label)


s, h, b = req("GET", "/healthz")
check("healthz 200", s == 200, s)
s, h, b = req("GET", "/")
check("SPA root 200", s == 200, s)
sec = [k for k in h if k.lower() in {
    "content-security-policy", "strict-transport-security", "x-content-type-options",
    "referrer-policy", "permissions-policy", "x-frame-options"}]
check("security headers 6/6", len(sec) == 6, sorted(k.lower() for k in sec))
check("no server version leak", "/" not in h.get("Server", h.get("server", "")), h.get("Server", ""))
s, _, _ = req("GET", "/suites")
check("deep link 200", s == 200, s)
s, _, _ = req("GET", "/api/v1/me")
check("api unauth 401", s == 401, s)
s, _, _ = req("GET", "/mcp/")
check("mcp GET unauth 401", s == 401, s)
s, _, _ = req("POST", "/mcp/", body={})
check("mcp POST unauth 401", s == 401, s)
s, _, _ = req("GET", "/api/v1/openapi.json")
check("openapi gated 404", s == 404, s)
s, _, b = req("GET", "/docs")
check("/docs is SPA shell", s == 200 and b"swagger" not in b.lower(), s)

if PAT:
    s, _, b = req("GET", "/api/v1/me", auth=True)
    me = json.loads(b) if s == 200 else {}
    check("me 200 (PAT)", s == 200, f"role={me.get('role')} admin={me.get('is_workspace_admin')}")
    name = me.get("display_name")
    if name:
        s, _, _ = req("PATCH", "/api/v1/me", auth=True, body={"display_name": name})
        check("PATCH /me 200 (write probe)", s == 200, s)
    s, _, b = req("GET", "/api/v1/connections", auth=True)
    conns = json.loads(b) if s == 200 else []
    items = conns.get("items", conns) if isinstance(conns, dict) else conns
    check("connections 200", s == 200, f"{len(items)} connections")
    for c in items:
        print(f"      conn {c.get('id')} {c.get('type'):<14} {c.get('name')}")
    mh = {"Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}
    s, rh, b = req("POST", "/mcp/", auth=True, headers=mh, body={
        "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
        "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
                   "clientInfo": {"name": "smoke", "version": "1"}}})
    sid = rh.get("mcp-session-id") or rh.get("Mcp-Session-Id")
    check("mcp initialize 200", s == 200 and bool(sid), s)
    if sid:
        mh["mcp-session-id"] = sid
        req("POST", "/mcp/", auth=True, headers=mh,
            body={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
        s, _, b = req("POST", "/mcp/", auth=True, headers=mh,
                      body={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/list"})
        text = b.decode()
        payload = text.split("data:", 1)[1] if "data:" in text else text
        tools = json.loads(payload).get("result", {}).get("tools", [])
        check(f"mcp tools/list = {EXPECT_TOOLS}", len(tools) == EXPECT_TOOLS, len(tools))

print(f"\n{len(fails)} failure(s): {fails}")
sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

excluded, still being seen) gets one suite with ``origin='auto'`` and no human owner, holding
ordinary checks that report change against the table's own history: row count, freshness and
column-profile anomaly, and schema drift. The daily reconciler only ever ADDS what is missing:
it never edits an existing check, never recreates one a person deleted, and pauses (never
deletes) the suites of tables that stop being covered.
"""

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/5ffbb754-c47f-4bef-b45f-a36850170a48/scratchpad/autoverify.py <<'EOF'
import json, os, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
FE = os.environ["FE"].rstrip("/"); H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['PAT']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
def call(m, p, body=None):
    r = urllib.request.Request(FE + p, method=m, headers=H, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=300) as x: return x.status, json.loads(x.read() or b"null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"null")
_, su = call("GET", "/api/v1/suites?limit=200"); su = su.get("items", su) if isinstance(su, dict) else su
auto = [s for s in su if s["name"].startswith("Auto: ")]
print("auto suites visible:", len(auto))
pick = None
for s in auto:
    _, sg = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/suggestions")
    if sg and len(sg) >= 2: pick = (s, sg); break
s, sg = pick
print("suite", s["name"], "pending suggestions", len(sg))
_, cs = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/checks"); cs = cs.get("items", cs) if isinstance(cs, dict) else cs
print("checks:", [(c["name"], c.get("kind"), c.get("check_type")) for c in cs])
a, b = sg[0], sg[1]
st, ra = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{a['id']}/accept"); print("accept", st, a["name"], "-> check", ra.get("check_id"))
st, rr = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{b['id']}/reject"); print("reject", st, b["name"], rr.get("status"))
st, again = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{a['id']}/accept"); print("re-accept (expect refusal)", st, str(again)[:150])
st, run = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/run", {}); rid = run.get("run_id") or run.get("id"); print("run", st, rid)
for _ in range(60):
    time.sleep(10); _, r = call("GET", f"/api/v1/runs/{rid}")
    if r["status"] not in ("queued", "running"): break
print("run", r["status"], f"{r['checks_passed']}/{r['checks_total']}", r.get("failure_reason"))
names = {c["id"]: c["name"] for c in cs}; _, cs2 = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/checks"); cs2 = cs2.get("items", cs2) if isinstance(cs2, dict) else cs2
names.update({c["id"]: c["name"] for c in cs2})
for x in r["results"]:
    print(f"   {x['status']:<6} {names.get(x['check_id'],'?'):<30} metric={x.get('metric_value')} obs={json.dumps(x.get('observed_value'), default=str)[:200]}")
EOF

import json, os, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
FE = os.environ["FE"].rstrip("/"); H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['PAT']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
def call(m, p, body=None):
    r = urllib.request.Request(FE + p, method=m, headers=H, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=300) as x: return x.status, json.loads(x.read() or b"null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"null")
_, su = call("GET", "/api/v1/suites?limit=200"); su = su.get("items", su) if isinstance(su, dict) else su
auto = [s for s in su if s["name"].startswith("Auto: ")]
print("auto suites visible:", len(auto))
pick = None
for s in auto:
    _, sg = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/suggestions")
    if sg and len(sg) >= 2: pick = (s, sg); break
s, sg = pick
print("suite", s["name"], "pending suggestions", len(sg))
_, cs = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/checks"); cs = cs.get("items", cs) if isinstance(cs, dict) else cs
print("checks:", [(c["name"], c.get("kind"), c.get("check_type")) for c in cs])
a, b = sg[0], sg[1]
st, ra = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{a['id']}/accept"); print("accept", st, a["name"], "-> check", ra.get("check_id"))
st, rr = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{b['id']}/reject"); print("reject", st, b["name"], rr.get("status"))
st, again = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suggestions/{a['id']}/accept"); print("re-accept (expect refusal)", st, str(again)[:150])
st, run = call("POST", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/run", {}); rid = run.get("run_id") or run.get("id"); print("run", st, rid)
for _ in range(60):
    time.sleep(10); _, r = call("GET", f"/api/v1/runs/{rid}")
    if r["status"] not in ("queued", "running"): break
print("run", r["status"], f"{r['checks_passed']}/{r['checks_total']}", r.get("failure_reason"))
names = {c["id"]: c["name"] for c in cs}; _, cs2 = call("GET", f"/api/v1/suites/{s['id']}/checks"); cs2 = cs2.get("items", cs2) if isinstance(cs2, dict) else cs2
names.update({c["id"]: c["name"] for c in cs2})
for x in r["results"]:
    print(f"   {x['status']:<6} {names.get(x['check_id'],'?'):<30} metric={x.get('metric_value')} obs={json.dumps(x.get('observed_value'), default=str)[:200]}")
EOF

class CheckDryRunRequest(ApiRequestModel):
    kind: str = "expectation"
    expectation_type: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    # Evaluating engine (ADR 0036); default 'gx'. #1530: a dmf preview must route through the
    # connection's native runner, not the GX one.
    engine: str = Field(default="gx", min_length=1, max_length=32)
    # The target comes from the suite's own run target (#215/#532) — resolved server-side exactly
    # like a persisted run.


class CheckDryRunResult(ApiModel):
    # pass | warn | fail | critical (ADR 0005), plus the two OPERATIONAL statuses: `error` (the
    # check could not be evaluated, #122) and `skip` (its precondition was not met, #593).
    status: str
    metric_value: float | None
    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None
    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None


@router.post(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/checks/dryrun",
    response_model=CheckDryRunResult,
    summary="Dry-run a check against live data (no persistence)",
)
def dry_run_check(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    payload: CheckDryRunRequest,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
    secret_store: Annotated[SecretStore, Depends(get_secret_store)],
) -> CheckDryRunResult:

    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
    assert connection is not None
    outcome = dryrun.dry_run_check(
        connection,
        session=db,

def _dry_run_anomaly(
    connection: Connection,
    *,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    target: dict[str, Any] | None,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
) -> DryRunOutcome:
    """Preview an anomaly check (#593): take the live measurement, score it against
    the history the check would have, and report the outcome — writing nothing.
    """
    from backend.app.datasources.monitors import (
        ANOMALY,
        MonitorConfigError,
        anomaly_params,
        monitor_outcome,
    )
    from backend.app.services import anomaly as anomaly_service

    try:
        params = anomaly_params(config)
    except MonitorConfigError as exc:
        raise DryRunUnsupportedError(str(exc)[:500], detail={"kind": ANOMALY}) from exc
    resolved = run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, target)
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    try:
        value = anomaly_service.measure_metric(
            connection,
            table=resolved.table,
            schema=resolved.schema,
            catalog=resolved.catalog,
            params=params,
            secret_store=secret_store,
            now=now,
        )
    except MonitorConfigError as exc:
        # DataQ-authored and safe to echo (a bad column, a non-SQL datasource, an
        # empty table) — the actionable half of a failed preview.
        raise DryRunFailedError(str(exc), detail={"table": resolved.table}) from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning(
            "dry_run_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
        )
        raise DryRunFailedError(
            "dry run could not measure the anomaly target metric",
            detail={"table": resolved.table, "reason": safe_failure_reason(exc)},
        ) from exc
    payload = anomaly_service.build_score_payload(value, [], params)
    payload["dry_run"] = True
    payload["preview"] = (
        "the baseline is learned from persisted runs; this check stays skipped until it "
        f"has {params.min_points} observations"
    )
    outcome = monitor_outcome(ANOMALY, scalar=payload, config=config, now=now)
    # No thresholds: the preview's status comes from the outcome's own operational state (`skip`).
    status, metric = resolve_status(
        outcome, warn_threshold=None, fail_threshold=None, critical_threshold=None
    )
    return DryRunOutcome(
        status=status,
        metric_value=metric,
        observed_value=sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value),
        expected_value=sanitize_json(outcome.expected_value),
    )

input.command:
cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --milestone "v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down" --label "bug,priority/P2" --title "Dry-running a column_profile anomaly check 502s: 'invalid freshness column identifier: None'" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What
Previewing an anomaly check with `target_metric: column_profile` (`POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun`) fails with **502 `dry_run_failed`: "invalid freshness column identifier: None"**. Found live on 2026-09-30 against the deployed Azure app, on both a Snowflake and a Unity Catalog suite (#2224 walkthrough).

## Why
`dryrun_service._dry_run_anomaly` calls `anomaly.measure_metric`, which has two branches: `row_count`, and everything else treated as **freshness**. `column_profile` falls into the freshness branch with no `column`, so building the statement fails. The run path is unaffected, because it measures `column_profile` through `measure_column_profile` / `_column_profile_outcome`. The same check runs correctly in a real suite; it did so on AWS's automatic suites the same day. Only the author's preview is broken, and it is broken for exactly the check automatic coverage adds to every suite.

## Fix
Give the preview a `column_profile` branch that takes the measurement the run path takes and reports the cold-start `skip` preview, like the other anomaly targets. Add a regression test that fails without it.
EOF
gh issue create --milestone "v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down" --label "bug,priority/P3" --title "AWS stack sets SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME to a secret it never creates, so every alert logs workspace_webhook_unresolved" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What
`deploy/terraform/aws/ecs.tf` hardcodes `SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME = "channel-slack-webhook"`, but the stack creates no such secret in Secrets Manager (only `dataq/channel-email-password` exists). Every alert on the live AWS deployment logs `workspace_webhook_unresolved` (channel `slack`) at WARNING, and Slack is silently off. Seen 3× after the 2026-09-30 walkthrough runs.

## Why it matters
A warning on every alert trains a reader to skip warnings on that stream. The configured name also implies that a Slack channel is wired when it is not. The email channel shows the right pattern: it derives from a variable (`var.alert_email`) and an empty value leaves it off.

## Fix
Make the Slack secret name a variable, defaulting to empty (channel off). Mirror it for Teams if the same shape exists. Document it in the AWS README.
EOF
gh issue create --milestone "v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down" --label "bug,priority/P3" --title "Alert builder calls session.get(User, None) for automatic suites (SAWarning, a future SQLAlchemy error)" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What
`backend/app/alerting/builder.py` `_resolve_owner` falls back to `session.get(User, suite.created_by)`. Automatic-coverage suites (ADR 0047) have **no human owner**, so `created_by` is NULL. SQLAlchemy then emits `SAWarning: fully NULL primary key identity cannot load any object. This condition may raise an error in a future release.` Seen on the live AWS worker on 2026-09-30, while building alerts for runs.

## Why it matters
Today it returns `None`, the right answer, but only by way of a deprecated path. A future SQLAlchemy release that raises here would break alert building for every automatic suite.

## Fix
Return `None` when `suite.created_by` is `None` without calling `session.get`. Add a test for an ownerless suite that fails without the fix, for example by turning warnings into errors.
EOF

- **Scratch stack:** API + worker on 127.0.0.1:8011 against a fresh database `dataq_gate2230`, PAT-only auth (OTP mode with a dummy mailer, no dev bypass, so the tunnel URL alone granted nothing).   - Role assignment: `Key Vault Secrets User` for `dataq-harness-adf`'s managed identity, scoped to that one secret.

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --milestone "v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down" --label "bug,priority/P2" --title "Alert says 'a manual or scheduled run' for a pipeline-triggered run whose pipeline run isn't recorded yet" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What
The failure email for an ADF-gate-triggered run (2026-09-30 walkthrough, suite `walkthrough 2026-09-30 gate fail`, incident `ca7f0113`) contradicts itself:
- **Run details → Triggered by: ADF** (from `run.triggered_by = adf:dataq_gate_fail:<run id>`).
- **Check card → Triggered by: "A manual or scheduled run (no upstream pipeline)."**

The second statement is false: the run was triggered by an ADF pipeline.

## Why
`incident_evidence._upstream_pipeline_layer` returns `None` in two different situations:
1. The run has no orchestration marker: a manual or scheduled run.
2. The run **has** an orchestration marker, but `markers.unambiguous_pipeline_run` finds no `pipeline_runs` row. The gate (ADR 0046) and the callback path create the DataQ run before the poller records the pipeline run; a marker collision also returns `None` here.

`render.py` (card line and `_upstream_pipeline_clause`), the RCA prompt (`llm_rca.py`) and the MCP `get_incident` docstring all read `None` as situation 1. The same null means two things, so the evidence states a confident falsehood on the surface where the trigger matters most.

## Fix
When the marker names an orchestration provider but the pipeline run can't be resolved, return a layer built from the marker itself (provider, pipeline id, provider run id) and say the pipeline run isn't recorded (or is ambiguous), instead of `None`. Render it as "ADF pipeline `dataq_gate_fail` (its run isn't recorded in DataQ yet)". Keep `None` for runs with no orchestration marker. Update the RCA prompt and the MCP docstring to match. Add regression tests that fail without the fix.
EOF

    curl -sf --max-time 30 -X PATCH "$AIRFLOW_URL/api/v1/dags/$d?update_mask=is_paused" \

      [[ "$state" != "queued" && "$state" != "running" && "$state" != "unknown" ]] && break

"""The `runs.triggered_by` ↔ `pipeline_runs` correlation, in ONE place (#1728).

`orchestration_service._trigger_suites` stamps a triggered run with
``f"{provider}:{pipeline_or_dag_id}:{provider_run_id}"``. Neither id is colon-free
(an Airflow ``run_id`` carries timestamps, dbt's job_name is free-form webhook
input), so the marker cannot be split back apart — and two distinct pipeline runs
can reconstruct to the identical string when a colon lands on the other side of
the boundary (``"nightly:etl"``+``"run-1"`` vs ``"nightly"``+``"etl:run-1"``).
Every reader therefore reconstructs-and-compares against the stored columns and
FAILS CLOSED when more than one row matches (#1714), instead of attributing a DQ
run to whichever row came back first.

Both directions are indexed (#1715): marker -> `pipeline_runs` by the
`ix_pipeline_runs_marker` expression index (#1814), marker -> `runs` by
`ix_runs_triggered_by`. Neither index can be made UNIQUE — a colliding marker is
legitimate input, and a unique index would refuse the INSERT instead of letting
the reader fail closed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections.abc import Collection, Iterable, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from sqlalchemy import ColumnElement, Select, func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.db.models import PipelineRun, Run

log = get_logger(__name__)


def pipeline_run_marker(pipeline_run: PipelineRun) -> str:
    return (
        f"{pipeline_run.provider}:{pipeline_run.pipeline_or_dag_id}:{pipeline_run.provider_run_id}"
    )


def _reconstructed_marker() -> ColumnElement[str]:
    # `||`, not concat(): textually the expression `ix_pipeline_runs_marker` is built on (#1814).
    return (
        PipelineRun.provider
        + ":"
        + PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id
        + ":"
        + PipelineRun.provider_run_id
    )


def pipeline_runs_for_marker_statement(marker: str) -> Select[tuple[PipelineRun]]:
    """Served by ``ix_pipeline_runs_marker`` (#1814); the provider pre-filter stays as a
    cheap second candidate for the planner.
    """
    provider, _sep, _rest = marker.partition(":")
    return select(PipelineRun).where(
        PipelineRun.provider == provider, _reconstructed_marker() == marker
    )


def pipeline_runs_for_marker(session: Session, marker: str) -> list[PipelineRun]:
    """Every stored pipeline run that reconstructs to ``marker`` — the caller decides
    what more than one means (nothing, for every reader today).
    """
    if ":" not in marker:
        return []
    return list(session.scalars(pipeline_runs_for_marker_statement(marker)))


def unambiguous_pipeline_run(session: Session, marker: str) -> PipelineRun | None:
    candidates = pipeline_runs_for_marker(session, marker)
    if len(candidates) == 1:
        return candidates[0]
    if candidates:
        log.warning("pipeline_run_marker_ambiguous", marker=marker, candidate_count=len(candidates))
    return None


def ambiguous_markers(session: Session, markers: Iterable[str]) -> set[str]:

    db_session: Any, world: dict[str, Any]
) -> None:
    """dbt's `pipeline_or_dag_id` (job_name) is free-form webhook input with no
    colon restriction (backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py), so two DISTINCT
    PipelineRun rows can reconstruct to the identical marker string when a
    colon lands on a different side of the pipeline/run-id boundary:
    ("nightly:etl", "run-1") and ("nightly", "etl:run-1") both concat to
    "dbt:nightly:etl:run-1". Neither row is unambiguously "the" match — the
    layer must return None (evidence unavailable) rather than silently
    attributing the incident to whichever row Postgres happens to return
    first.
    """

                started_at=now - timedelta(minutes=5),

                started_at=now - timedelta(minutes=5),
                finished_at=now - timedelta(minutes=4),
